sanskrit: सत्त्वं सुखे सञ्जयति रजः कर्मणि भारत । ज्ञानमावृत्य तु तमः प्रमादे सञ्जयत्युत ॥
hindiTranslation: हे भरतवंशोद्भव अर्जुन  सत्त्वगुण सुखमें और रजोगुण कर्ममें लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजय करता है तथा तमोगुण ज्ञानको ढककर एवं प्रमादमें भी लगाकर मनुष्यपर विजंय करता है ॥
englishTranslation: Sattva binds through pleasure, rajas through action, and tamas, covering knowledge, binds through negligence.
essence: Each force traps you in a different way: comfort, activity, or blindness.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Three forces shape human behavior differently: one lures with pleasure, one drives constant activity, and one hides understanding while pulling a person into carelessness.
simpleInsight: It becomes easier to notice what is steering you before it quietly takes over.
detailedMeaning: Krishna explains the three forces that shape every mind and action. This verse shows how each force captures a person in a different way: pleasure, restless doing, or dull confusion.
modernRelevance: Three friends miss the same deadline: one was lost in a good book, one took on too many jobs, one simply drifted. Krishna gives each a different hook: pleasure, busyness, negligence.
translationLiteral: सत्त्वम् (sattva) / सुखे (in pleasure) / सञ्जयति (binds) / रजः (rajas) / कर्मणि (in action) / भारत (O Bharata) / ज्ञानम् (knowledge) / आवृत्य (covering) / तु (but) / तमः (tamas) / प्रमादे (in negligence) / सञ्जयति (binds) / उत (also)
insight: Krishna sums up the binding in one line: pleasure for sattva, action for rajas, negligence for tamas.

quoteVariants.text: Pleasure can bind you. Action can bind you. Confusion binds hardest.
Pleasure binds. Action binds. Confusion blinds.
Even comfort can trap me, not just chaos.
See the bindings before they move you.
